newsitem.title: ZAIRE: Zaireans say children seized as war hostages.
newsitem.headline: Zaireans say children seized as war hostages.

text.p: Zairean villagers said on Thursday Rwandan Hutu fighters seized their children as hostages and took them to the vast Mugunga refugee camp near Goma in the east Zaire war zone.

Two mothers told Reuters they lost 12 children to Hutu kidnappers. The director of a local school said about 100 children in all had been taken in the days before their village fell into the hands of rival Tutsi rebels this week.
Aid agencies left the area after serious fighting last week so no independent confirmation was possible.

"The Interahamwe (Hutu rebels) came to our house on Saturday. They forced my family to leave the village and took all eight of my children with them as hostages to Mugunga camp," said Suzanne Damukunzi, 45.
Their village is some eight km (five miles) outside Goma, a city seized by Tutsi rebels last week.
Two km (one mile) on the other side of the frontline is Mugunga, which was the world's largest refugee camp last week crammed with 400,000 Rwandan Hutu refugees including Interahamwe militiamen.

Villagers said the Hutu rebels killed at least 12 more of their children in fighting. They said bodies still lay in no man's land, 300 metres (yards) away amid banana plantations and eucalyptus trees.
Elisabeth Huyimana said the Rwandan Hutus, who had lived in camps in the Goma area for more than two years before the latest fighting erupted, had come to her home on Sunday.
"They tried to cut my stomach open with a knife but it didn't work. I fell to the ground and they took four of my children with them as hostages," she said.
"Around 100 children have been taken to Mugunga from here," local school director Evariste Nkundiye told Reuters in the centre of the village where parents had gathered for safety.
"They know that if children are taken as hostages nobody will attack the camp."
No Tutsi rebels were present when the villagers spoke out.
Interahamwe extremist Hutu militiamen had a leading role in the 1994 genocide in Rwanda of up to one million Tutsis and Hutu moderates and are fighting the advance of the Tutsi rebels in Zaire.
The villagers identify themselves as Zairean Hutus.
"The Interahamwe want to make us know that we will all have to die together," said Yuma Urimubenshi, who had three children taken.
The villagers insist that the Tutsi fighters in the area are members of Rwanda's regular army, despite official Rwandan denials. But some Rwandan troops entered Goma last week.

Despite a one-sided ceasefire declared by the rebels on Monday, mortars and anti-aircraft gunfire were heard from the area north of Mugunga as night fell and witnesses said fighting raged earlier on Thursday along the front line.
The Rwandan government says it wants 1.1 million of its Hutus who fled to Zaire in 1994 to come home. But the Interahamwe say they cannot return because they will be jailed or killed.
African leaders say a key to ending conflict lies in separating innocent refugees at Mugunga and elsewhere from the the armed "intimidators" who will not let them go home.
"They are turning Mugunga into a hostage camp," Keshero orphanage director Floribert Makongo said.
